order.rule: pairs alternate analog-first / biased-first so neither group is systematically earlier in the run sequence

scale_justification.conclusion: under a per-event CV between 0.1 and 0.3 the design resolves relative differences of roughly 0.2% to 0.7% at 99% confidence; differences below that are only declared compatible at this resolution, never equivalent
scale_justification.kind: pre-registered design prior, not a measured result
scale_justification.method: group mean = mean of 16 independent batch means; each 2000-event batch mean has relative standard error CV/sqrt(2000); the group mean then has relative SE divided by sqrt(16); a Welch 99% interval for the difference has half-width t*sqrt(2)*group SE
scale_justification.resource_basis: 32 runs x 2000 events on the same host, 2 threads, serial launch; comparable frozen Q2 cases of 2000 events ran in the low single-digit seconds on this host, so the whole campaign is a minutes-scale run. No wall-clock number is promised by this draft.

biasing_rule.expected_observations: The biased group must contain at least one finite, positive hit weight different from 1 and a worker receipt with applied_callbacks>0; the analog group must keep unit hit weights. No fixed discrete weight values and no interaction-count probabilities are required or predicted. A batch lacking the non-unit-weight signature is a failed batch.
biasing_rule.no_weight_prediction_limit: The radiation length of G4_Pb is not the eBrem mean free path, and the 5 mm centre-to-boundary distance is not enough to infer how many interactions occur; only the kernel run can establish that.
biasing_rule.weight_observation: The implementation uses G4BOptnChangeCrossSection: the operation proposes a cross-section change, and the weight actually assigned to a track depends on which operations the kernel proposes and applies and on transport that survives without an interaction. A factor=10 cross-section ratio therefore does NOT determine a complete-track weight set. The realized weights must be observed from the run's own hits/phase-space evidence and the worker receipts; they are not predicted by this draft.

boundaries: this draft does not run, seed, bootstrap or inspect the biasing case results
one rule on one primary electron; no claim about other particles, processes, materials, geometries, factors or secondary biasing
the interval is a finite-sample compatibility statement, not a proof of global unbiasedness or equivalence
no product code, tests, frozen references, tables or phase files are touched

geometry_facts.source_to_boundary: the point source sits at the centre, so a forward primary has 5 mm to the nearest boundary; this is a geometry fact only and is not used to predict the number of interactions
geometry_facts.target: 10 mm cube, G4_Pb, sensitive=true, bias=true, centred at origin
geometry_facts.target_local_frame: world frame (no translation in the geometry file)

common_inputs.output: CSV; --output and --seed are command-line arguments so the two config files stay byte-identical except the gate
common_inputs.physics: FTFP_BERT with default_cut 0.1 mm; the biased group additionally enables the generic-biasing wrapping
common_inputs.scoring: explicitly enabled=true, hits=true, event_edep=true, dose=true; let=false, fluence=false, edep=false; auto_create_default_scorers=true; no mesh. The Dose scorer is enabled explicitly, not through a default, and the configuration-phase facts must confirm it.
common_inputs.source: one primary: e-, 10 MeV, point (0,0,0) mm, direction (0,0,1)

covers: both rendered configs carry the explicit scoring flags (dose=true, let=false, fluence=false) and differ only in the biasing gate
the --inspect-run facts (configuration phase only, execution_performed=false) report those scoring fields as consumed and the expected biasing gate difference; inspection never stands in for a run

counterexamples_for_execution: CE-ANALOG-REGISTERED: copy the biased config as the analog run (or the reverse) and require EP-WORKER-EVIDENCE to fail
CE-WEIGHT-MISSING: delete all non-unit-weight hits from a copy of a biased batch and require EP-WEIGHT-NONUNIT to fail
CE-WORKER-RECEIPT-MISSING: remove worker receipts from a copy and require EP-WORKER-EVIDENCE to fail
CE-DROP-EVENT-ROW: delete one event row from a copy and require EP-EVENT-ROWS to fail
CE-ANALOG-WEIGHT: alter an analog hit weight to 0.1 in a copy and require EP-WEIGHT-NONUNIT to fail
CE-STATS-S2: alter sum_sq in a copy and require EP-STATS-RECON to fail
CE-DROP-BATCH: drop the worst pair from a copy of the analysis and require the analysis driver to refuse (frozen batch list is the only allowed input)

efficiency.conditions: same host, 2 threads, serial launch, equal event budget per run
efficiency.fom: FOM = 1/(R^2 * run_wall_time_s) per run, recomputed from the printed moments and time; no fabricated zero or guessed time
efficiency.report: group means/medians of time and FOM, batch-level distribution, and the statement that equal or worse efficiency is a valid result
efficiency.timing_source: scorer_statistics.csv run_wall_time_s (production field); host wall clock recorded by the execution driver separately and never substituted for the production field

execution_plan.authorization: requires a separate reviewed decision; this draft is not authorization to simulate
execution_plan.run_sequence: seed-order.json runs list, executed in order; each run gets its own output directory under runs/<batch>/output
execution_plan.stop_rule: stop the campaign at the first failed batch and keep raw evidence

failure_and_limited_rules: backend exit nonzero, status != completed, missing summary/event/statistics file, completed_events != 2000, missing event rows, non-finite numbers, missing/duplicated worker receipts, missing non-unit weight signature, or non-approximate uncertainty status => batch fails; no replacement batch and no resampling is allowed
a batch whose evidence is incomplete is reported as failed, not silently replaced by remaining batches; the campaign stops and the raw evidence is kept
statistical anomaly (batch mean far from its group) is reported descriptively and never converted into a backend-defect claim

analog.note: analog means no biasing operator is registered at all; this is not factor=1, which would still wrap and change the weight arithmetic

out_of_scope_suggestions: secondary biasing and per-process factor scans are separate preregistrations
a full XS audit (table provenance and physical evaluation) belongs to the independent NIEL/XS audit track, not to this weight-arithmetic test
if the campaign shows a resolution-limited result, sizing a follow-up needs a new frozen design rather than extending this one

decision_rules.anomaly: any batch with missing evidence, non-finite values or failed checks stops the comparison; batches are never dropped, and anomalous batch means are listed descriptively, not tested pairwise for significance
decision_rules.compatible: interval contains 0: report 'no difference beyond the preset error at this resolution'; this is not equivalence and not evidence of global unbiasedness
decision_rules.degenerate: zero standard error: report an exact arithmetic result under the frozen model only; no 99% coverage claim
decision_rules.detected: interval excludes 0: report a difference at this resolution; do not attribute it to a backend defect and do not call the bias factor wrong

limitations: 16 batches per group: the Welch interval is a finite-sample approximation whose coverage is not exact under non-normal or unequal-variance data
batch means are independent by construction (distinct seeds); this is not a paired shared-random-numbers design
only one primary comparison is allowed; per-pair or repeated tests are not performed and cannot be reported as a significance result
time order is balanced but cannot exclude slow drift; the order list is fixed and not re-randomised after seeing data
primary_comparison.test: one two-sided Welch 99% interval for (mean_biased - mean_analog) over the 16 independent batch means per group

primary_endpoint.batch_moments: S=sum D_i; S2=sum D_i^2; R=sqrt(S2/S^2 - 1/N); sigma_event=R*mean_b
checks: EP-EVENT-ROWS: the union of event IDs across worker event_edep files is exactly 0..1999; every batch has N=2000 rows; a missing row is a failure
EP-MASS: dose CSV mass_kg equals rho*V using G4_Pb density 11.35 g/cm3 and V=1 cm3 within the 12-digit half-unit interval; the CSV value is primary
EP-DOSE-RECON: sum of weighted dose rows across workers equals sum_i D_i within the half-unit interval plus the stated accumulation bound
EP-STATS-RECON: statistics S, S2, R for weighted dose equal the values recomputed from the event rows (R=sqrt(S2/S^2-1/N)); entries equals the number of nonzero-dose events
EP-WEIGHT-POSITIVE: every nonzero hit weight is finite and >0; sum of hit weighted_edep equals event weighted_edep within rounding

EP-SCORING-ENABLED: the effective configuration facts must show scoring.enabled=true, hits=true, event_edep=true, dose=true, let=false, fluence=false and auto_create_default_scorers=true; relying on the default dose=false is a failed input (the defect the v1 review found)

EP-WEIGHT-NONUNIT: biased group must show at least one finite positive hit weight != 1 in every batch; analog group must show weight == 1 on every hit; a missing signature fails the batch. No particular discrete weight value is required because the realized weights are kernel outcomes, not cross-section arithmetic

EP-WORKER-EVIDENCE: each biased run has a real [G4USimBiasing] worker receipt per (run,thread) with operators=1, matched_rules=1, tls_verified, end_run_completed, proposals>0 and no failure; the analog run must report no attached biasing operator, not biasing_effect_observed
EP-NO-UNKNOWN: biasing_effect_observed=unknown or configuration acceptance alone is never accepted as weight evidence
primary_endpoint.per_batch_formula: mean_b = (1/N) * sum_i D_i; N=2000; zero-deposition events are kept and enter the mean as 0
primary_endpoint.quantity: per-completed-event weighted deposited dose in Target, Gy/event

sources.dose_summary: dose_volume_summary_tN.csv: mass_kg, weighted_dose_Gy, weighted_edep_MeV, weighted_edep_sum_sq_MeV2, n_events
sources.event_edep: event_edep_tN.csv: runID,eventID,raw_edep_MeV,weighted_edep_MeV; one row per completed event including zero deposition
sources.hits: hits_tN.csv: observed deposition steps with weight; a witness of emitted steps and weights, not a complete event or scoring-step set
sources.statistics: scorer_statistics.csv: total row for weighted dose with n_events, entries, value, sum, sum_sq, rel_error, uncertainty_estimator, uncertainty_status

checks.detail: t quantile decreases with df toward the normal limit
Student-t includes zero while a normal-quantile rule would reject
half width equals critical * standard error
event-level pseudo SE=1.581e-05 vs batch SE=7.071e-04 (~1/sqrt(2000))
dropping the worst batch changes the interval, so it is a forbidden post-hoc choice
identical constant batches are degenerate, not 'no difference proven'
zero-variance group gives df=15 and a finite Welch interval
infinite batch means raise instead of producing a finite-looking interval
16x2000 batches resolve sub-percent differences under the stated CV priors
batch seeds do not intersect the frozen/used Q2 seed inventory
16 complete pairs, one run per group

covers: Student-t quantile from an independent incomplete-beta implementation against published constants and the normal limit

negative controls: normal quantile instead of t at the boundary changes the decision; event-level pseudo-replication understates the error; dropping the worst batch changes the interval; zero variance is not equivalence; infinite batch means are rejected
seed table uniqueness/disjointness and balanced run order
pure_math.does_not_cover: No assumption about realized track-weight values, interaction counts or survival probabilities is made or tested here; those are execution observations, not mathematical identities.

reproduction: execution (only after independent review): see proposal.execution_plan
scope_statement: Preregisters one XS-biasing versus analog comparison on a single 1 cm lead cube with 10 MeV electrons. The expected observable is the track-weight change produced by one bremsstrahlung rule on the primary; the comparison is the weighted deposited dose per completed event. Only the linear weight arithmetic of a registered biasing operation is exercised.
